clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within three years: your grandfather Clifford's return to the family in early 1989, your move to the rebuilt Hollin Road house in autumn 1989, your late nights and shift away from chess and debate, your mother filling in your college forms while you underfunctioned, your wrist injury in October 1991 that stopped your playing, your blow-up with Rafe and his move out, your days getting high and absorbed in fixing radios, your low functioning and high anxiety through 1992, your grandmother Winifred's thyroid surgery around the same time, your wedding of your parents to Desmond in October 1992, and your feeling stung that your dad had not heard of your film in early 1994. These shifts cluster around the loss and the household's settling after it, with your functioning wavering through the period as you moved between conservatory, home, and college.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within two and a half years: your running out of steam for performing and your disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002, your shift away from your family and friends, your move to Gull Harbour, your meeting Marisol and moving to Fenwick in 2003, your separation from her within the year, your sinking into deep depression once you split, your distance from your parents who seemed a world away from what you were going through, your turn toward friends Corbin, Dale and Silas, and your grandmother's death of the cancer in February 2004. Your functioning fell and your anxiety rose through these years; the period settles as you began swimming and returned to your therapist in early 2004.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within a year and a half: your four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek in July 2008 where you were too drained for conversation, your mother pressing to visit despite your saying the timing was wrong, your keeping the door shut on her and the visit going wrong, your stopping all speech with your mother when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in August 2008, a silence that held roughly a year, and your aunt Imogen's stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation. Your distance from your mother piled up across these months, with your anxiety rising as she pushed and you pulled away. The cutoff that began at the lodge deepened and held until your functioning began to recover through 2009.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within nearly three years: your seeing your mother a bit less once Wren came along, your cousin Alice diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your sister Tara flying for the airline and marrying James, your aunt Imogen's memory slipping and worsening since 2015 and her lashing out when muddled by October 2018, your cousin Hal driving her most of her care, your mother having a heart check-up and clearing it, a street party and fundraising dinner and drive to the lake for your mother-in-law Frances's retirement in October 2019 that left your partner Wren swamped with one thing after another, your overfunctioning too strictly with a plan to settle her, her close talks all day with her father and brother in fusion while you felt you did not belong, your waking from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and pulling back as the others rose, and the long quiet drives home afterward with Wren anxious. Your symptoms rose and your functioning dipped around the family occasion; Wren's symptom and anxiety rose and her functioning fell around the same time, shifting in opposite ways. These months gather around the shift in your own household and the pressures on Wren's side of the family.
